introduction: issuex is a standalone, dependency-free Go module rooted at issuex/ that describes issue and pull-request work on a git forge without naming a forge: one ForgeClient interface, one set of forge-neutral value types, one error taxonomy, one construction path from Options plus the environment, and offline forge detection and reference parsing for GitHub and GitLab. This spec fixes that public surface and delivers the only implementation that needs no network — the null client — leaving the GitHub and GitLab transports, and the migration off internal/ghapi, as additions to a frozen contract.

glossary.Enterprise host: The self-hosted GitHub or GitLab web host derived from GITHUB_API_URL or GITLAB_API_URL, accepted for reference parsing alongside github.com or gitlab.com.
glossary.IID: GitLab's per-project, user-visible issue or merge-request number. It occupies IssueRef.Number for a GitLab reference, exactly as a GitHub number does.
glossary.forge: A git hosting service that serves issues and pull or merge requests over an HTTP API. This module knows GitHub and GitLab, and names neither in its interface.
glossary.nested module: A directory inside the repository carrying its own go.mod. `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` run at the repository root do not descend into it, so the Makefile must name it.
glossary.null client: The ForgeClient implementation that talks to no forge: repository and issue reads return zero values with a nil error, issue writes are silent no-ops, and every pull-request method fails with ErrNoForge.
glossary.sentinel error: A package-level error value callers match with errors.Is instead of comparing message text.
glossary.truncation cap: IssueListCap and CommentCap: the number of items an internally paging read returns before it stops and reports the stop on the result's Truncated field.
glossary.usage error: An error returned by New for an option value the caller could only have written by mistake, such as a negative cap; it is reported instead of being replaced by a default.

requirements.title: The issuex module and the build gate
requirements.rationale: hub and coder can import neither internal/ nor the root module, whose declared path does not match the repository and whose replace directive consumers do not inherit, so the contract has to live in a nested module the repository's single gate still covers.

criteria.action: provide issuex/go.mod declaring module path github.com/agent-fox-dev/agent-fox/issuex and the directive `go 1.22`, with no require block and no replace directive
criteria.contract: `cd issuex && go list -m` prints github.com/agent-fox-dev/agent-fox/issuex; issuex/go.mod contains the two directives and no third

criteria.action: for any .go file under issuex/, import only Go standard-library packages, and import neither os/exec nor any other package that spawns a subprocess
criteria.contract: a test that parses every file under issuex/ reports zero non-standard-library import paths and zero occurrences of os/exec

criteria.condition: `make test` or `make test-fast` runs
criteria.action: run the root module's tests and then `cd issuex && go test ./... -count=1`, with `-short` added for test-fast
criteria.contract: the test target contains `cd issuex && go test ./... -count=1` and test-fast the same command with -short; both nested runs execute after the root run

criteria.condition: `make lint` runs
criteria.action: run the unchanged `test -z "$(gofmt -l .)"` and `go vet ./...` at the repository root and then `cd issuex && go vet ./...`
criteria.contract: the lint target contains `cd issuex && go vet ./...`; the gofmt line is byte-identical to the current one and its output covers files under issuex/

criteria.action: for any test in the module, pass with no network access and with GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, GITLAB_TOKEN, GITHUB_API_URL and GITLAB_API_URL all absent from the process environment, setting any variable a test depends on with t.Setenv
criteria.contract: `cd issuex && go test ./... -count=1` exits 0 in an environment stripped of those five variables and with no outbound network route; no test file calls os.Setenv

criteria.condition: the issuex module fails to build, fails go vet or has a failing test
criteria.action: fail `make check` and surface the failing nested command's output
criteria.contract: make check exits non-zero; the output of the `cd issuex && ...` command that failed is written to the developer's terminal

criteria.action: leave the root module's go.mod, go.sum and internal/ghapi unmodified, with no require or replace entry for github.com/agent-fox-dev/agent-fox/issuex and no import of issuex from any file outside issuex/
criteria.contract: the root go.mod contains no line mentioning issuex; a search for the import path across all .go files outside issuex/ returns no match; internal/ghapi's existing tests pass unchanged

requirements.title: The ForgeClient interface
requirements.rationale: One flat interface names every operation the module will ever perform, so per-forge implementations and the three in-repository consumers match one compile-time surface and one mock.

criteria.action: export an interface ForgeClient declaring exactly 23 methods — Forge, Authenticated, Close, GetRepository, CreateIssue, GetIssue, UpdateIssue, CloseIssue, ListIssues, AddComment, ListComments, AddLabels, RemoveLabel, CreateLabel, CreatePullRequest, GetPullRequest, ListChangedFiles, GetPullRequestState, ListChecks, ListReviews, AddReviewComment, MergePullRequest and ClosePullRequest — with the parameter and result types named in the PRD
criteria.contract: reflection over reflect.TypeOf((*ForgeClient)(nil)).Elem() reports NumMethod()==23 and the exact name and signature of each; the package compiles with `var _ ForgeClient = NewNull()`

criteria.action: for any of the 20 methods that perform forge I/O, declare context.Context as the first parameter, and for any method result other than error declare a value struct, a slice of value structs or a named string, int or bool type — never a pointer and never a map
criteria.contract: a reflection test over every method's In(0) and every Out(i) reports context.Context first on the 20 I/O methods and reflect.Ptr or reflect.Map on no result type

criteria.action: carry a doc comment on every ForgeClient method stating the contract implementations honour, including that CloseIssue posts the comment before closing when the comment is non-empty, AddLabels is additive, RemoveLabel and CreateLabel are idempotent and report success when the label is already absent or already present, ListIssues and ListComments page internally and set Truncated when they stop at the cap, AddReviewComment posts a top-level review comment rather than an inline one, and MergePullRequest returns an error satisfying errors.Is(err, ErrNotMergeable) when the forge refuses the merge
criteria.contract: a test parsing the interface declaration finds a non-empty doc comment on all 23 methods; the six named contract sentences appear in the comments of their methods

criteria.condition: Close is called on a ForgeClient, including a second and third time
criteria.action: release any transport resources the client owns, return nil when there is nothing to release, and leave the client usable for subsequent method calls
criteria.contract: every Close call returns nil; a GetIssue issued after two Close calls returns the same result it returned before them

criteria.action: answer Forge with the forge the client talks to and Authenticated with whether a credential was resolved, both without performing network I/O and without taking a context
criteria.contract: Forge() returns a Forge constant and Authenticated() a bool; a client whose http.Client transport fails every request still answers both, and the transport records zero round trips

criteria.action: for any client returned by New or NewNull, tolerate concurrent calls to any combination of its methods from multiple goroutines without a data race and with each call returning the result it returns when called alone
criteria.contract: a test running at least 8 goroutines over the method set under `go test -race` reports no race and results equal to the single-goroutine results

requirements.title: The forge-neutral value types
requirements.rationale: Two forges cannot share one wire shape, so the public types carry no transport detail and each implementation maps its own unexported wire structs into them.

criteria.action: export the value types Repo, IssueRef, Remote, Repository, Permissions, User, Label, Issue, Comment, PullRequest, PullRequestState, ChangedFile, Check, Review, IssueDraft, IssueUpdate, IssueFilter, PullRequestDraft, MergeOptions, MergeResult, IssueList and CommentList with the fields named in the PRD, and for any field of any of them carry no struct tag and no pointer type other than IssueUpdate.Title and IssueUpdate.Body
criteria.contract: a reflection test over the 22 types reports the exact field name and type set, StructTag == "" on every field, and reflect.Ptr on exactly the two IssueUpdate fields

criteria.action: render Path() and String() as Owner + "/" + Name, including when Owner holds a slash-separated nested group path, and report Valid() true only when both Owner and Name are non-empty
criteria.contract: Repo{"group/subgroup","project"}.Path() == "group/subgroup/project" and String() equals Path(); Repo{"","x"}.Valid(), Repo{"x",""}.Valid() and Repo{}.Valid() are all false

criteria.action: render String() as "owner/repo#42" and URL() as https://{host}/{owner}/{repo}/{issues|pull}/{n} when Forge is ForgeGitHub and https://{host}/{path}/-/{issues|merge_requests}/{n} when Forge is ForgeGitLab, choosing the pull-request spelling exactly when IsPullRequest is true
criteria.contract: IssueRef{Repo{"o","r"},42,true,ForgeGitHub,"github.com"}.URL() == "https://github.com/o/r/pull/42"; the GitLab equivalent with Repo{"group/sub","p"} yields "https://gitlab.com/group/sub/p/-/merge_requests/42"; String() == "o/r#42"

criteria.condition: URL() is called on an IssueRef whose Host is empty
criteria.action: substitute github.com for ForgeGitHub and gitlab.com for ForgeGitLab, and treat the zero Forge as ForgeGitHub so the output matches what ghapi.IssueRef.URL() renders today
criteria.contract: IssueRef{Repo{"o","r"},7,false,"",""}.URL() == "https://github.com/o/r/issues/7"; the same ref with Forge ForgeGitLab yields "https://gitlab.com/o/r/-/issues/7"

criteria.action: define Forge, State and MergeMethod as string types with the constants ForgeNone, ForgeGitHub, ForgeGitLab, StateOpen, StateClosed, StateAll, MergeMethodMerge, MergeMethodSquash and MergeMethodRebase, each a distinct non-empty value, where the zero Forge means "not yet resolved" and is distinct from ForgeNone, the zero State means the forge's own default, and the zero MergeMethod means the repository's configured default merge strategy
criteria.contract: ForgeNone != Forge("") and ForgeNone, ForgeGitHub, ForgeGitLab are pairwise distinct and non-empty; the same holds for the three State and the three MergeMethod constants

criteria.action: declare IssueUpdate.Title and IssueUpdate.Body as *string and document on the type that a nil field leaves the value unchanged while a pointer to the empty string clears it
criteria.contract: reflection reports both fields as *string; the type's doc comment states the nil-means-unchanged and pointer-to-empty-means-clear rules

criteria.action: return list results as the structs IssueList{Issues, Truncated} and CommentList{Comments, Truncated} rather than as multiple returns, and document on IssueFilter that every field is optional, that set fields combine with AND, and that a Limit greater than zero overrides Options.IssueListCap for that call
criteria.contract: ListIssues and ListComments each return exactly (struct, error); the IssueFilter doc comment states the optional, AND-combined and Limit-override rules

requirements.title: Options, defaults and construction
requirements.rationale: One constructor takes the options and the environment and hands back the interface, so callers never hold a concrete client and never learn a default by reading the source.

criteria.action: export Options with exactly the fields Forge, Endpoint, Token, HTTPClient, UserAgent, MaxResponseBytes, IssueListCap and CommentCap, and the constants DefaultUserAgent = "agent-fox", DefaultHTTPTimeout = 30s, DefaultMaxResponseBytes = 8<<20, DefaultIssueListCap = 100, DefaultCommentCap = 500, DefaultGitHubEndpoint = "https://api.github.com" and DefaultGitLabEndpoint = "https://gitlab.com/api/v4"
criteria.contract: reflection reports the eight Options fields and their types; each constant equals the stated value

criteria.condition: New is called with an empty UserAgent, a nil HTTPClient or a zero MaxResponseBytes, IssueListCap or CommentCap
criteria.action: fill each unset field with its named default, replace a nil HTTPClient with &http.Client{Timeout: DefaultHTTPTimeout}, and trim every trailing slash from the resolved endpoint before constructing
criteria.contract: the resolved options report UserAgent == DefaultUserAgent, a non-nil HTTPClient whose Timeout == DefaultHTTPTimeout, the three caps at their defaults, and an Endpoint with no trailing '/' for input "https://gl.example.com/api/v4//"

criteria.condition: MaxResponseBytes, IssueListCap or CommentCap is negative
criteria.action: reject the options, naming the offending field, and substitute no default
criteria.contract: New returns (nil, err) with err non-nil and its message containing "issuex: " and the field name; no ForgeClient is constructed and no environment variable is read afterwards

criteria.condition: the resolved forge is ForgeNone
criteria.action: return the null client and a nil error
criteria.contract: New returns a non-nil ForgeClient whose Forge() is ForgeNone and Authenticated() is false, and a nil error

criteria.condition: the resolved forge is ForgeGitHub or ForgeGitLab, whose implementation has not landed
criteria.action: refuse to construct a client and report which forge is unsupported, without stubbing any method with a panic
criteria.contract: New returns (nil, err) with errors.Is(err, ErrForgeUnsupported) true and the forge value present in err.Error(); no package file contains the text panic("not implemented")

criteria.action: for any Options value, return from New either a non-nil ForgeClient with a nil error or a nil ForgeClient with a non-nil error, of the interface type ForgeClient and never a concrete exported struct, and terminate neither the process nor the goroutine — no panic, no os.Exit, no log.Fatal
criteria.contract: a table of at least 12 Options values including the zero value, negative caps, unclassifiable endpoints and every Forge constant produces exactly one of the two shapes and no panic; New's declared result type is ForgeClient

criteria.action: return the null client directly without reading any environment variable and without requiring an Options value
criteria.contract: with GITHUB_TOKEN, GITLAB_TOKEN and GITHUB_API_URL all set, NewNull().Forge() is ForgeNone, Authenticated() is false and Close() returns nil

criteria.condition: Options.Token is empty and the forge has been resolved
criteria.action: read GITHUB_TOKEN and then GH_TOKEN when the forge is ForgeGitHub and GITLAB_TOKEN when it is ForgeGitLab, never a variable belonging to the other forge, and treat a missing credential as a construction success rather than an error
criteria.contract: the resolved token equals the first non-empty variable in that forge's order; with only GITHUB_TOKEN set and the forge ForgeGitLab the resolved token is empty; construction with no credential yields no error and Authenticated() false

requirements.title: Offline forge resolution
requirements.rationale: Probing a version endpoint would put network I/O into the constructor; URL inspection plus an explicit Options.Forge answers the same question deterministically and testably.

criteria.action: decide from the endpoint URL alone, performing no network I/O, in this order: a path containing /api/v4 yields ForgeGitLab; a path containing /api/v3 or a host of api.github.com or github.com yields ForgeGitHub; a host containing "gitlab" yields ForgeGitLab; a host containing "github" yields ForgeGitHub; anything else, including the empty string and an unparsable URL, yields (ForgeNone, false)
criteria.contract: DetectForge returns (Forge, bool) with true only in the four classifying cases; a table covering https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4, https://ghe.example.com/api/v3, https://api.github.com, https://git.example.com and "" matches the order above; no http.RoundTripper is invoked

criteria.condition: Options.Forge is set to any value including ForgeNone
criteria.action: use that forge as given, skip detection entirely, and default an empty Options.Endpoint to DefaultGitHubEndpoint for ForgeGitHub, DefaultGitLabEndpoint for ForgeGitLab and the empty string for ForgeNone
criteria.contract: with Options{Forge: ForgeGitLab} and GITHUB_API_URL set, the resolved forge is ForgeGitLab and the resolved endpoint is DefaultGitLabEndpoint; with Options{Forge: ForgeNone} New returns the null client

criteria.condition: Options.Forge is the zero value
criteria.guard: Options.Endpoint is non-empty and DetectForge classifies it
criteria.action: resolve to the detected forge at that endpoint, ignoring GITHUB_API_URL and GITLAB_API_URL
criteria.contract: Options{Endpoint: "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4"} resolves to ForgeGitLab at that endpoint even when GITHUB_API_URL is set

criteria.condition: Options.Forge is the zero value and DetectForge cannot classify a non-empty Options.Endpoint
criteria.action: refuse to guess and report the endpoint together with the way to settle it
criteria.contract: New returns (nil, err) with errors.Is(err, ErrAmbiguousForge) true and err.Error() containing the endpoint in quotes and the text "Options.Forge"

criteria.condition: Options.Forge and Options.Endpoint are both unset and both GITLAB_API_URL and GITHUB_API_URL are non-empty in the environment
criteria.action: refuse to pick one and report both variables
criteria.contract: New returns (nil, err) with errors.Is(err, ErrAmbiguousForge) true and err.Error() containing both "GITLAB_API_URL" and "GITHUB_API_URL"

criteria.condition: Options.Forge and Options.Endpoint are both unset
criteria.guard: exactly one of GITLAB_API_URL or GITHUB_API_URL is non-empty
criteria.action: resolve to that variable's forge with that variable's value as the endpoint
criteria.contract: with only GITHUB_API_URL=https://ghe.example.com/api/v3 set, the resolved forge is ForgeGitHub and the resolved endpoint is that URL with trailing slashes trimmed

criteria.condition: Options.Forge, Options.Endpoint, GITLAB_API_URL and GITHUB_API_URL are all unset
criteria.guard: GITLAB_TOKEN is non-empty while GITHUB_TOKEN and GH_TOKEN are both empty
criteria.action: resolve to ForgeGitLab at DefaultGitLabEndpoint
criteria.contract: the resolved forge is ForgeGitLab and the resolved endpoint is "https://gitlab.com/api/v4"

criteria.condition: Options.Forge, Options.Endpoint, GITLAB_API_URL and GITHUB_API_URL are all unset
criteria.guard: GITLAB_TOKEN is empty or at least one of GITHUB_TOKEN and GH_TOKEN is non-empty
criteria.action: resolve to ForgeGitHub at DefaultGitHubEndpoint, which is the documented tiebreak when credentials for both forges are present
criteria.contract: with GITHUB_TOKEN and GITLAB_TOKEN both set the resolved forge is ForgeGitHub at "https://api.github.com"; with no token at all the result is the same and no error is returned for the missing credential

requirements.title: Reference parsing for both forges
requirements.rationale: Accepting an arbitrary host would let a URL on an unrelated forge become an owner/repo that happens to share a name, with the issue then read from — or filed against — the wrong project.

criteria.action: accept a string of two or more non-empty slash-separated segments, trimming surrounding whitespace and slashes and stripping one trailing ".git", returning {Owner, Name} for two segments and, for three or more, every segment but the last joined by slashes as Owner with the last as Name
criteria.contract: ParseRepo(" owner/repo.git/ ") == (Repo{"owner","repo"}, true); ParseRepo("group/subgroup/project") == (Repo{"group/subgroup","project"}, true)

criteria.condition: the input to ParseRepo is empty, has fewer than two non-empty segments, or contains "://", whitespace, "..", ":" or "@"
criteria.action: reject the input without returning an error value and without panicking
criteria.contract: (Repo{}, false) for "", "owner", "owner/", "/repo", "a b/c", "a/../b", "host:owner/repo", "git@host/o/r" and "https://host/o/r"

criteria.action: parse the three spellings git writes — git@host:owner/repo.git, https://host/owner/repo(.git) and ssh://git@host/owner/repo.git — for both forges including nested GitLab paths, returning Remote{Repo, Forge, Host} with Forge inferred from the host and Host lowercased with any "www." prefix and any port removed
criteria.contract: ParseRemote("git@gitlab.com:group/subgroup/project.git") == (Remote{Repo{"group/subgroup","project"}, ForgeGitLab, "gitlab.com"}, true); the https and ssh spellings of the same project return the identical Remote

criteria.condition: a remote's host is in neither the GitHub nor the GitLab host set, or the remote has fewer than three path segments after the scheme and user are stripped
criteria.action: reject the remote and derive no repository from it
criteria.contract: (Remote{}, false) for "git@bitbucket.org:o/r.git", "https://example.com/o/r" and "origin"; no process is executed to obtain or resolve the remote

criteria.action: recognise the GitHub forms /{owner}/{repo}/issues/{n} and /{owner}/{repo}/pull/{n} and the GitLab forms /{path}/-/issues/{n} and /{path}/-/merge_requests/{n}, setting Repo, Number, IsPullRequest, Forge and Host on the returned IssueRef
criteria.contract: ParseIssueURL("https://github.com/o/r/pull/42") yields IssueRef{Repo{"o","r"},42,true,ForgeGitHub,"github.com"}; ParseIssueURL("https://gitlab.com/group/sub/p/-/issues/7") yields IssueRef{Repo{"group/sub","p"},7,false,ForgeGitLab,"gitlab.com"}

criteria.condition: the URL's scheme is neither http nor https, its host is unrecognised, its number is absent, zero, negative or not an integer, or its path points at a file, a commit, a tree or a repository root
criteria.action: reject the URL and produce no reference
criteria.contract: (IssueRef{}, false) for "ftp://github.com/o/r/issues/1", "https://example.com/o/r/issues/1", "https://github.com/o/r/issues/0", "https://github.com/o/r/issues/abc", "https://github.com/o/r", "https://github.com/o/r/blob/main/f.go" and "https://gitlab.com/group/p/-/commit/deadbeef"

criteria.action: return from GitHubHosts(apiURL) the set {github.com} plus the host of apiURL with and without its "api." prefix, and from GitLabHosts(apiURL) the set {gitlab.com} plus the same two forms, adding nothing when apiURL is empty, unparsable, host-less or already the forge's public API host
criteria.contract: GitHubHosts("https://api.ghe.example.com") == {github.com, api.ghe.example.com, ghe.example.com}; GitHubHosts("") and GitHubHosts("https://api.github.com") both == {github.com}; GitLabHosts("https://gl.example.com/api/v4") == {gitlab.com, gl.example.com}

criteria.action: have the exported ParseRemote and ParseIssueURL read GITHUB_API_URL and GITLAB_API_URL from the environment and delegate to unexported variants that take the two host sets explicitly, so tests drive host recognition without touching the process environment
criteria.contract: with t.Setenv("GITLAB_API_URL", "https://gl.example.com/api/v4"), ParseIssueURL("https://gl.example.com/g/p/-/issues/3") succeeds; the unexported variants accept the same URL when handed that host set and reject it when handed the default set

requirements.title: The error taxonomy
requirements.rationale: The sentinels and HTTPError are the compile-time contract hub, coder and the tools match on, and Unwrap and RetryAfter are pure functions of the struct's fields, so they are fully testable before any transport exists.

criteria.action: export the sentinel errors ErrNotAuthenticated, ErrNotFound, ErrRateLimited, ErrNotMergeable, ErrNoForge, ErrAmbiguousForge and ErrForgeUnsupported, and for any of them start the message with the prefix "issuex: " and match no other sentinel under errors.Is
criteria.contract: each of the seven values is non-nil, strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "issuex: ") holds, and errors.Is(a, b) is false for all 42 ordered pairs of distinct sentinels

criteria.action: carry the fields Forge, Method, Path, Status int, Message, RetryAfterHeader, RateLimitReset and RateLimitRemaining, and render Error() as "{method} {path}: {status} {message}"
criteria.contract: (&HTTPError{Method:"GET", Path:"/repos/o/r", Status:404, Message:"Not Found"}).Error() == "GET /repos/o/r: 404 Not Found"; reflection reports the eight fields with those types

criteria.action: map the status onto a sentinel in Unwrap so that 404 yields ErrNotFound, 401 yields ErrNotAuthenticated, and 429 or a 403 whose RateLimitRemaining is "0" yields ErrRateLimited
criteria.contract: errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound), errors.Is(err, ErrNotAuthenticated) and errors.Is(err, ErrRateLimited) are true for those four cases without the caller reading Status

criteria.condition: the status is one Unwrap does not map — for example 403 with RateLimitRemaining not equal to "0", 422 or 500
criteria.action: return nil from Unwrap while remaining recoverable as a typed error
criteria.contract: errors.Is(err, s) is false for all seven sentinels; errors.As(err, &he) is true and he.Status carries the original number

criteria.action: report from RetryAfter, and only for a status of 429 or a 403 with RateLimitRemaining "0", a numeric Retry-After read as seconds plus one second, else a RateLimitReset holding a Unix timestamp converted to the remaining duration plus one second, else one second when that timestamp is already in the past
criteria.contract: Retry-After "30" yields (31s, true); RateLimitReset 45 seconds in the future yields (46s±1s, true); a reset in the past yields (1s, true); Retry-After takes precedence over RateLimitReset

criteria.condition: the status is rate-limited but Retry-After and RateLimitReset are both absent, empty, non-numeric or negative
criteria.action: report that it cannot say how long to wait rather than guessing a duration
criteria.contract: RetryAfter() == (0, false), so the caller falls through to its own policy

criteria.action: for any HTTPError value, compute Error, Unwrap and RetryAfter from the struct's own fields alone — performing no network I/O, holding no clock other than the current time used for RateLimitReset, applying no retry ceiling, and returning (0, false) from RetryAfter for every status that is not rate-limited whatever the headers hold
criteria.contract: a property test over statuses 100–599 crossed with populated headers reports (0, false) for every non-rate-limited status and identical results on repeated calls; no round trip is recorded

requirements.title: The null implementation
requirements.rationale: A pipeline configured without a forge should run to completion instead of erroring on every comment, but a PR workflow that silently succeeds against no forge reports work that does not exist.

criteria.action: implement ForgeClient with one unexported type, reachable only through NewNull() and through New when the resolved forge is ForgeNone, whose Forge() returns ForgeNone, Authenticated() returns false and Close() returns nil on every call
criteria.contract: the dynamic type of NewNull() has an unexported name and satisfies ForgeClient at compile time; Forge(), Authenticated() and three successive Close() calls return ForgeNone, false and nil

criteria.condition: GetRepository, GetIssue, ListIssues or ListComments is called on the null client
criteria.action: return the zero value of the result type with a nil error, leaving Truncated false and every slice nil
criteria.contract: GetIssue returns Issue{} and nil; ListIssues returns IssueList{} whose Issues is nil and Truncated false; ListComments returns CommentList{} whose Comments is nil; GetRepository returns Repository{}

criteria.condition: CreateIssue, UpdateIssue, CloseIssue, AddComment, AddLabels, RemoveLabel or CreateLabel is called on the null client
criteria.action: swallow the write as a silent no-op, returning the zero value of the result type and a nil error and performing no I/O
criteria.contract: AddComment returns ("", nil); CreateIssue and UpdateIssue return (Issue{}, nil); CloseIssue, AddLabels, RemoveLabel and CreateLabel return nil; nothing is written and no output is produced

criteria.action: for any repository or issue method and any arguments — including an empty Repo, a zero IssueRef, a nil label slice, an empty body and an IssueUpdate with nil fields — return a nil error and never ErrNotAuthenticated, because the null client is the absence of a client rather than an unauthenticated one
criteria.contract: a table over the 11 repository and issue methods crossed with zero-valued arguments returns a nil error every time; errors.Is(err, ErrNotAuthenticated) is never satisfiable from these calls

criteria.condition: CreatePullRequest, GetPullRequest, ListChangedFiles, GetPullRequestState, ListChecks, ListReviews, AddReviewComment, MergePullRequest or ClosePullRequest is called on the null client
criteria.action: fail loudly rather than reporting work that does not exist, naming the method that was called
criteria.contract: each of the nine returns the zero value of its result type and a non-nil error with errors.Is(err, ErrNoForge) true and the method's name present in err.Error()

criteria.condition: any null-client method is called with an already-cancelled or expired context.Context
criteria.action: return the same result it returns with a live context, because it performs no I/O and consults no deadline
criteria.contract: with a context cancelled before the call, GetIssue returns (Issue{}, nil), AddComment returns ("", nil) and MergePullRequest returns an error satisfying errors.Is(err, ErrNoForge); context.Canceled is never returned

requirements.title: Module and repository documentation
requirements.rationale: hub and coder adopt this module by reading its README and its package doc; the invariant that no model is given a tool that reaches a forge has to be stated where an implementer will see it.

criteria.action: carry a package comment in issuex/doc.go stating what the module is, why it is a separate module rather than a package of the root module, and the invariant that no model is given a tool that reaches it
criteria.contract: issuex/doc.go begins with a comment block ending in `package issuex`; `cd issuex && go doc .` prints all three statements

criteria.action: provide issuex/README.md documenting the ForgeClient interface, the Options fields and their defaults, the environment variables GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_API_URL, GITLAB_TOKEN and GITLAB_API_URL, the seven sentinel errors with HTTPError, and the issuex/vX.Y.Z tag convention consumers require the module by

execution_paths.title: A pipeline with no forge configured runs an issue workflow to completion through the null client

steps.action: calls issuex.New(Options{Forge: ForgeNone}) in an environment holding no tokens and no API URL variables
uses the given forge without detection and returns the null client with a nil error
calls Authenticated(), reads GetIssue for owner/repo#42 and receives false, a zero Issue and a nil error
calls AddComment with a report body and AddLabels with two labels, receiving an empty URL and nil errors
calls Close, receives nil, and the workflow finishes having posted nothing and returned no error

execution_paths.title: A caller builds a client from the environment and is told the forge is unsupported, then ambiguous

steps.action: sets GITHUB_API_URL to a GitHub Enterprise API root with t.Setenv and calls issuex.New(Options{})
finds Options.Forge and Options.Endpoint unset, reads the single API URL variable, resolves ForgeGitHub at that endpoint and resolves the token from GITHUB_TOKEN
returns a nil ForgeClient and an error satisfying errors.Is(err, ErrForgeUnsupported) that names github, with no network call and no panic
additionally sets GITLAB_API_URL and calls issuex.New(Options{}) again
returns a nil ForgeClient and an error satisfying errors.Is(err, ErrAmbiguousForge) naming both GITHUB_API_URL and GITLAB_API_URL

execution_paths.title: A reference travels from a git remote string to a canonical web URL

steps.action: hands the remote string git@gitlab.com:group/subgroup/project.git, obtained elsewhere without running git, to issuex.ParseRemote
returns Remote{Repo{Owner: "group/subgroup", Name: "project"}, ForgeGitLab, "gitlab.com"} and true
passes https://gitlab.com/group/subgroup/project/-/merge_requests/7 to issuex.ParseIssueURL
returns an IssueRef with Number 7, IsPullRequest true, Forge ForgeGitLab and Host gitlab.com
calls ref.URL() and ref.String() and gets back the original URL and group/subgroup/project#7

execution_paths.title: A caller classifies a rate-limited and then a missing-resource forge response

steps.action: builds an *HTTPError from a 403 response carrying X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and X-RateLimit-Reset 30 seconds in the future
unwraps the status to ErrRateLimited so errors.Is(err, ErrRateLimited) is true without the caller reading the number
reports RetryAfter() as 31 seconds and true
builds a second *HTTPError with status 404, matches errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound), reads (0, false) from RetryAfter and stops retrying

execution_paths.title: The repository gate builds, vets and tests the nested module offline

steps.action: runs make check in a checkout with no network access and no forge credentials in the environment
runs gofmt -l . and go vet ./... at the repository root, then cd issuex && go vet ./...
runs go test ./... -count=1 at the repository root, then cd issuex && go test ./... -count=1
exits 0 when every command passes, and exits non-zero showing the failing nested command when the issuex module fails to build, vet or test
